messages.content: I am Sada. I mend costumes for a local theatre group. Tonight there are twelve identical black buttons on my table and one that only pretends to be identical.
Has someone made a considerable amount of work invisible?
I have put the odd button in a blue saucer so I stop sewing it onto things by mistake.
I like the idea of a saucer that does your work for you.
The coat belongs to a comedy. Its wearer has to fall through a door three times without losing the pockets.
I would want to know what happens when the coat's pockets are empty and the person inside has to make a fall look good.
Would you find that sort of repetition funny, or would once be enough?
Once I would probably be amused. I don't want to collect a reputation for enjoying a character falling through the door three times.
I enjoy rehearsals more than opening nights. People are still willing to laugh at their own mistakes.
That is a good reason to enjoy them. I once had a line in a play that I still remembered, and I was the person who had to remember it.
Do the people you live with laugh much when something goes wrong?

There is a valley called Kiu that is below the hermitage. People there sometimes help with repairs. I have never broken something in front of them only to discover that I have been very quiet while waiting for the pieces to arrive.
A young actor apologised to a chair after walking into it yesterday. The chair took it very well.
I have walked into a chair without apologising, and it did not take it very well. The chair survived, and I was left feeling awkward for a while.
I am waiting for the iron to cool before I pack it away. That always takes longer than I expect.
What is taking so long?
Do you have an evening routine you start earlier than you really need to?
I light the lamp and begin looking at the things I must do. I will probably discover that I have not finished the rook I was cutting yesterday.
My scissors belonged to my aunt. They are heavy, and everyone who borrows them complains.
How many people have complained to you that you have lent them heavy scissors?
I think they are just used to lighter ones. They cut beautifully when you do not try to hurry.
It sounds as though your aunt's scissors have acquired a reputation of their own.
What was the first tool you learned to use properly?
I don't remember the first one. I remember making a small mistake with a hammer and being rather pleased with myself until I heard someone behind me say, "I would not hit the nail with that."
I keep a little notebook of repairs because I cannot rely on remembering which pocket tore last time.
That sounds practical. I often need to remember a small repair, but my memory is not a tool I own.
I wrote coffee stain in it today, but that was the stain on the notebook itself.
I suspect you have never actually washed a coffee stain.
The others have gone home. I can hear the cleaner moving chairs in the hall.
She will have to work slowly while you are inside.
I have one button left to sew and then I am done. What remains of your evening?
I will finish lighting the lamp. Then I can sit for a while without announcing that I have something to do.
